findings.description: __aexit__ calls self.__exit__ with (None, None, None) instead of forwarding exc_type, exc_value and traceback, so exceptions raised in the body are never recorded.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `async with attempt:` where the body raises. __exit__ is told there was no exception, so it calls set_result(None) and returns None. The exception then propagates out unrecorded and the retry logic never sees the failure. The retry state records a success, and the exception also bypasses retry handling. The sync __exit__ presumably calls set_exception when exc_type is set, which is skipped here.
